     estimator = SlidingEstimator(LinearDiscriminantAnalysis())
     cross_val_predict(estimator, X, y, method='predict_proba', cv=2)
+
+
+def _capture_stderr(callable_):
+    """Capture stderr from running callable_()."""
+    import io
+    import sys
+    captured = io.StringIO()
+    old_err = sys.stderr
+    sys.stderr = captured
+    try:
+        callable_()
+    finally:
+        sys.stderr = old_err
+    return captured.getvalue()
+
+
+@requires_sklearn
+def test_sliding_estimator_stores_verbose_attribute():
+    """The ``verbose`` constructor argument should be stored on the instance."""
+    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
+    sl = SlidingEstimator(LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear'),
+                          verbose=False)
+    assert hasattr(sl, 'verbose')
+    assert sl.verbose is False
+
+    gl = GeneralizingEstimator(LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear'),
+                               verbose=False)
+    assert hasattr(gl, 'verbose')
+    assert gl.verbose is False
+
+
+@requires_sklearn
+def test_sliding_estimator_verbose_false_silent_njobs1():
+    """SlidingEstimator(verbose=False, n_jobs=1) should not print anything."""
+    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
+    X, y = make_data()
+
+    def _run():
+        sl = SlidingEstimator(
+            LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear'),
+            n_jobs=1, verbose=False)
+        sl.fit(X, y)
+        sl.score(X, y)
+        sl.predict(X)
+
+    output = _capture_stderr(_run)
+    assert 'Fitting' not in output, output
+    assert 'Scoring' not in output, output
+    assert 'Transforming' not in output, output
+    assert '[Parallel' not in output, output
+
+
+@requires_sklearn
+def test_sliding_estimator_verbose_false_silent_njobs2():
+    """SlidingEstimator(verbose=False, n_jobs>1) should not print anything."""
+    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
+    X, y = make_data()
+
+    def _run():
+        sl = SlidingEstimator(
+            LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear'),
+            n_jobs=2, verbose=False)
+        sl.fit(X, y)
+        sl.score(X, y)
+        sl.predict(X)
+
+    output = _capture_stderr(_run)
+    assert 'Fitting' not in output, output
+    assert 'Scoring' not in output, output
+    assert 'Transforming' not in output, output
+    assert '[Parallel' not in output, output
+
+
+@requires_sklearn
+def test_generalizing_estimator_verbose_false_silent_njobs2():
+    """GeneralizingEstimator(verbose=False, n_jobs>1) should be silent too."""
+    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
+    X, y = make_data()
+
+    def _run():
+        gl = GeneralizingEstimator(
+            LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear'),
+            n_jobs=2, verbose=False)
+        gl.fit(X, y)
+        gl.score(X, y)
+        gl.predict(X)
+
+    output = _capture_stderr(_run)
+    assert 'Fitting' not in output, output
+    assert 'Scoring' not in output, output
+    assert 'Transforming' not in output, output
+    assert '[Parallel' not in output, output
+
+
+@requires_sklearn
+def test_sliding_estimator_score_no_joblib_messages_default():
+    """SlidingEstimator.score() should not leak joblib [Parallel] messages.
+
+    Aligns ``score`` with ``fit``/``_transform`` which already pass
+    ``verbose=False`` to ``parallel_func``.
+    """
+    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
+    X, y = make_data()
+
+    def _run():
+        sl = SlidingEstimator(
+            LogisticRegression(solver='liblinear'), n_jobs=2)

+        sl.score(X, y)
+
+    output = _capture_stderr(_run)
+    assert '[Parallel' not in output, output

+	BeforeEach(t)

+	start := time.Now()

+
+func TestPageWaitForResponseRespectsTimeoutOption(t *testing.T) {
+	BeforeEach(t)

+	_, err := page.Goto(server.EMPTY_PAGE)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	start := time.Now()
+	resp, err := page.WaitForResponse("**/never-fires-xyz", playwright.PageWaitForResponseOptions{
+		Timeout: playwright.Float(500),
+	})
+	elapsed := time.Since(start)

+	require.Nil(t, resp)

+}
+
+func TestPageWaitForRequestMatchingSucceeds(t *testing.T) {
+	BeforeEach(t)
+	defer AfterEach(t)
+	type result struct {
+		req playwright.Request
+		err error
+	}
+	ch := make(chan result, 1)
+	go func() {
+		r, e := page.WaitForRequest("**/empty.html", playwright.PageWaitForRequestOptions{
+			Timeout: playwright.Float(15000),
+		})
+		ch <- result{r, e}
+	}()
+
+	time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
+	_, err := page.Goto(server.EMPTY_PAGE)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	select {
+	case r := <-ch:

+		require.NotNil(t, r.req)
+		require.Contains(t, r.req.URL(), "empty.html")
+	case <-time.After(20 * time.Second):
+		t.Fatal("WaitForRequest did not return in time")
+	}
+}
+

expect_file() {
  local label=$1 file=$2 expected=$3

    || fail "$label: got [$(cat "$file")], want [$expected]"
}

expect_empty() {
  local label=$1 file=$2
  [ ! -s "$file" ] || fail "$label: got [$(cat "$file")]"

  local label=$1 command=$2 token_regex=$3

  awk -v command="$command" -v token_regex="$token_regex" '
    BEGIN { found = 0 }
    {
      lower = tolower($0)
      if (index(lower, command) && lower ~ token_regex && $0 ~ / - .+/)

}

      $3 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || $4 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || $5 !~ /^[-N]$/ { exit 1 }

}

+#include <errno.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+#include <sys/ipc.h>
+#include <sys/shm.h>
+
+int main(int argc, char **argv) {
+  key_t key;
+  int old_id;
+  int id;
+  void *ptr;
+
+  if (argc != 2) {
+    fprintf(stderr, "usage: make_bad_shm <key>\n");
+    return 2;
+  }
+
+  key = (key_t) strtol(argv[1], NULL, 10);
+  old_id = shmget(key, 0, 0);
+  if (old_id >= 0)
+    shmctl(old_id, IPC_RMID, NULL);
+
+  id = shmget(key, 4096, IPC_CREAT | IPC_EXCL | 0600);
+  if (id < 0) {
+    fprintf(stderr, "shmget: %s\n", strerror(errno));
+    return 1;
+  }
+
+  ptr = shmat(id, NULL, 0);
+  if (ptr == (void *) -1) {
+    fprintf(stderr, "shmat: %s\n", strerror(errno));
+    shmctl(id, IPC_RMID, NULL);
+    return 1;
+  }
+
+  memset(ptr, 0xa5, 4096);
+  shmdt(ptr);
+  return 0;
+}

diff --git a/usercase-test-coderl/test_dataclassio_json_helpers.py b/usercase-test-coderl/test_dataclassio_json_helpers.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/usercase-test-coderl/test_dataclassio_json_helpers.py
@@ -0,0 +1,428 @@
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import json
+import os
+import socket
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Annotated, Any
+
+import pytest
+
+from efro.dataclassio import (
+    EXTRA_ATTRS_ATTR,
+    IOAttrs,
+    dataclass_from_json,
+    dataclass_to_json,
+    ioprepped,
+)
+
+
+@ioprepped
+@dataclass
+class ScoreCard:
+    name: str
+    score: int
+
+
+@ioprepped
+@dataclass
+class OrderedCard:
+    zebra: int
+    alpha: int
+    mid: str
+
+
+@ioprepped
+@dataclass
+class FloatCard:
+    value: float
+    label: str = 'flt'
+
+
+@ioprepped
+@dataclass
+class NestedCard:
+    title: str
+    child: ScoreCard
+    tags: list[str]
+    meta: dict[str, int]
+    ratio: float
+
+
+@ioprepped
+@dataclass
+class StoredNameCard:
+    public_name: Annotated[str, IOAttrs('n')]
+    score: Annotated[int, IOAttrs('s')]
+
+
+@ioprepped
+@dataclass
+class AnyPayloadCard:
+    payload: Any
+
+
+@ioprepped
+@dataclass
+class FallbackCard:
+    class State(Enum):
+        KNOWN = 'known'
+        OTHER = 'other'
+
+    label: str
+    state: Annotated[State, IOAttrs('st', enum_fallback=State.OTHER)]
+
+
+def test_to_json_compact_default_separators() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = ScoreCard(name='bob', score=7)
+
+    actual = dataclass_to_json(obj)
+
+    assert actual == '{"name":"bob","score":7}'
+
+
+def test_to_json_pretty_sorts_keys_by_default() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = OrderedCard(zebra=2, alpha=1, mid='m')
+
+    actual = dataclass_to_json(obj, pretty=True)
+
+    assert actual == '{\n  "alpha": 1,\n  "mid": "m",\n  "zebra": 2\n}'
+
+
+def test_to_json_compact_sort_keys_true() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = OrderedCard(zebra=2, alpha=1, mid='m')
+
+    actual = dataclass_to_json(obj, sort_keys=True)
+
+    assert actual == '{"alpha":1,"mid":"m","zebra":2}'
+
+
+def test_to_json_pretty_sort_keys_false() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = OrderedCard(zebra=2, alpha=1, mid='m')
+
+    actual = dataclass_to_json(obj, pretty=True, sort_keys=False)
+
+    assert actual == '{\n  "zebra": 2,\n  "alpha": 1,\n  "mid": "m"\n}'
+
+
+def test_to_json_uses_json_codec_dict_conversion() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = NestedCard(
+        title='match',
+        child=ScoreCard(name='ana', score=11),
+        tags=['red', 'blue'],
+        meta={'wins': 3, 'losses': 1},
+        ratio=2,
+    )
+
+    actual = dataclass_to_json(obj)
+
+    assert (
+        actual
+        == '{"title":"match","child":{"name":"ana","score":11},'
+        '"tags":["red","blue"],"meta":{"wins":3,"losses":1},"ratio":2.0}'
+    )
+
+
+def test_to_json_uses_field_storage_names() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = StoredNameCard(public_name='bob', score=7)
+
+    actual = dataclass_to_json(obj)
+
+    assert actual == '{"n":"bob","s":7}'
+
+
+def test_to_json_forwards_coerce_to_float_true_default() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = FloatCard(value=2)
+
+    actual = dataclass_to_json(obj)
+
+    assert actual == '{"value":2.0,"label":"flt"}'
+
+
+def test_to_json_forwards_coerce_to_float_false_error() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = FloatCard(value=2)
+
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as excinfo:
+        dataclass_to_json(obj, coerce_to_float=False)
+
+
+    assert isinstance(excinfo.value, TypeError)
+
+
+def test_to_json_rejects_nonfinite_float_values() -> None:
+
+
+
+    obj = AnyPayloadCard(payload=float('nan'))
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
+        dataclass_to_json(obj)
+
+
+    assert isinstance(excinfo.value, ValueError)
+
+
+def test_from_json_returns_equal_dataclass_instance() -> None:
+
+
+
+    actual = dataclass_from_json(ScoreCard, '{"name":"bob","score":7}')
+
+    assert actual == ScoreCard(name='bob', score=7)
+
+
+def test_from_json_forwards_coerce_to_float_true_default() -> None:
+
+
+
+    actual = dataclass_from_json(FloatCard, '{"value":2}')
+
+    assert actual == FloatCard(value=2.0, label='flt')
+
+
+def test_from_json_forwards_coerce_to_float_false_error() -> None:
+
+
+
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as excinfo:
+        dataclass_from_json(FloatCard, '{"value":2}', coerce_to_float=False)
+
+
+    assert isinstance(excinfo.value, TypeError)
+
+
+def test_from_json_preserves_unknown_attrs_by_default() -> None:
+
+
+
+    actual = dataclass_from_json(
+        ScoreCard, '{"name":"bob","score":7,"nickname":"bobby"}'
+    )
+
+    assert actual == ScoreCard(name='bob', score=7)
+    assert getattr(actual, EXTRA_ATTRS_ATTR) == {'nickname': 'bobby'}
+
+
+def test_from_json_forwards_allow_unknown_attrs_false() -> None:
+
+
+
+    with pytest.raises(AttributeError) as excinfo:
+        dataclass_from_json(
+            ScoreCard,
+            '{"name":"bob","score":7,"nickname":"bobby"}',
+            allow_unknown_attrs=False,
+        )
+
+
+    assert isinstance(excinfo.value, AttributeError)
+
+
+def test_from_json_forwards_discard_unknown_attrs_true() -> None:
+
+
+
+    actual = dataclass_from_json(
+        ScoreCard,
+        '{"name":"bob","score":7,"nickname":"bobby"}',
+        discard_unknown_attrs=True,

+        )
+
+    def make_scalar_image(self, values):

+        return tio.ScalarImage(tensor=tensor)

+        transforms = [
+            tio.Clamp(out_min=-2.5, out_max=4.5),

+        ]
+        for transform in transforms:
+            self.assertTrue(callable(transform))
+

+        image = self.make_scalar_image([-7.0, -2.5, -1.25, 3.0, 4.5, 9.0])
+        transformed = tio.Clamp(out_min=-2.5, out_max=4.5)(image)
+        expected = torch.tensor(
+            [-2.5, -2.5, -1.25, 3.0, 4.5, 4.5],
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+        ).reshape(1, 1, 1, -1)

+

+        expected = torch.tensor([-1.5, -1.5, 0.0, 8.0]).reshape(1, 1, 1, -1)
+        self.assert_tensor_equal(transformed.data, expected)
+
+    def test_upper_only_clamp(self):

+    screen = pyte.DiffScreen(5, 3)

+
+
+

+

+
+    screen.dirty.clear()
+    assert screen.dirty == set([])
+
+    screen.draw(u"A")
+    assert screen.dirty == set([0])
+    assert screen.display == [u"A    ", u"     ", u"     "]
+
+    screen.draw(u"B")
+    assert screen.dirty == set([0])
+    assert screen.display == [u"AB   ", u"     ", u"     "]

+    screen.cursor_position(2, 3)

+    assert b.dirty == set([0, 1, 2])

+
+
+def test_caller_dirty_clear_is_idempotent_and_session_continues():
+
+
+
+    screen = pyte.DiffScreen(5, 3)
+
+    screen.dirty.clear()
+    screen.dirty.clear()
+    assert screen.dirty == set([])

+    screen = _seed_screen()

@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+import re
+
+from scrapy.crawler import Crawler
+from scrapy.pipelines import ItemPipelineManager
+from scrapy.utils.project import get_project_settings
+from twisted.internet.defer import Deferred
+from twisted.python.failure import Failure
+
+from locations.items import GeojsonPointItem
+from locations.spiders.greggs_gb import GreggsGBSpider
+
+
+def _deferred_result(result):
+    if not isinstance(result, Deferred):
+        return result
+    seen = []
+    result.addBoth(lambda value: seen.append(value) or value)
+    assert seen, "item pipeline processing did not complete synchronously"
+    value = seen[0]
+    if isinstance(value, Failure):
+        value.raiseException()
+    return value
+
+
+def _process_item(phone, country):
+    settings = get_project_settings().copy()
+    pipelines = settings.getdict("ITEM_PIPELINES")
+    pipelines.pop("locations.pipelines.ApplyNSICategoriesPipeline", None)
+    settings.set("ITEM_PIPELINES", pipelines)
+    crawler = Crawler(GreggsGBSpider, settings)
+    spider = GreggsGBSpider.from_crawler(crawler)
+    manager = ItemPipelineManager.from_crawler(crawler)
+    _deferred_result(manager.open_spider(spider))
+    item = GeojsonPointItem(
+        name="Test location",
+        ref=f"test-{country}-{phone}",
+        lat=51.5007,
+        lon=-0.1246,
+        phone=phone,
+        country=country,
+    )
+    try:
+        processed = _deferred_result(manager.process_item(item, spider))
+    finally:
+        _deferred_result(manager.close_spider(spider))
+    return processed, crawler.stats
+
+
+def _assert_normalized_international_phone(normalized, raw, country_code, national_digits):
+    assert normalized != raw
+    assert normalized.startswith(f"+{country_code}")
+    assert re.sub(r"\D", "", normalized) == country_code + national_digits
+
+
+def test_item_processing_normalizes_valid_phone_numbers_with_country_context():
+    examples = [
+        ("044 201 75 00", "CH", "41", "442017500"),
+        ("(248) 446-8015", "US", "1", "2484468015"),
+        ("020 7031 3000", "GB", "44", "2070313000"),
+        ("030 901820", "DE", "49", "30901820"),
+    ]
+
+    for raw_phone, country, country_code, national_digits in examples:
+        item, stats = _process_item(raw_phone, country)
+        normalized = item.get("phone")
+        _assert_normalized_international_phone(
+            normalized, raw_phone, country_code, national_digits
+        )
+        assert not stats.get_value("atp/field/phone/invalid")
+
+
+def test_item_processing_counts_phone_shaped_but_invalid_numbers():
+    for raw_phone in ("2434577249", "1234567890"):
+        item, stats = _process_item(raw_phone, "US")
+        assert stats.get_value("atp/field/phone/invalid", 0) >= 1

+import Router from '../../../src/index'
+
+
+
+
+function createMockApp (uid) {
+  const handlers = {}
+  return {
+    _uid: uid,
+    _isDestroyed: false,
+    $once (event, cb) {
+      handlers[event] = cb
+    },
+
+    $destroy () {
+      this._isDestroyed = true
+      const cb = handlers['hook:destroyed']
+      if (cb) cb()
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+function newRouter () {
+  return new Router({ mode: 'abstract', routes: [] })
+}
+
+describe('router.apps memory cleanup (issue #2639)', () => {
+  it('init() pushes the app into router.apps and sets router.app', () => {
+    const router = newRouter()
+    const app = createMockApp(1)
+
+    router.init(app)
+
+    expect(router.apps.length).toBe(1)
+    expect(router.apps[0]).toBe(app)
+    expect(router.app).toBe(app)
+  })
+
+  it('removes destroyed app from router.apps', () => {
+    const router = newRouter()
+    const app = createMockApp(1)
+
+    router.init(app)
+    expect(router.apps.length).toBe(1)
+
+    app.$destroy()
+
+    expect(router.apps.length).toBe(0)
+    expect(router.apps.indexOf(app)).toBe(-1)
+  })
+
+  it('sets router.app to null when the only app is destroyed', () => {
+    const router = newRouter()
+    const app = createMockApp(1)
+
+    router.init(app)
+    app.$destroy()
+
+    expect(router.app).toBe(null)
+  })
+
+  it('reassigns router.app to a remaining app when the main app is destroyed', () => {
+    const router = newRouter()
+    const main = createMockApp(1)
+    const secondary = createMockApp(2)
+
+    router.init(main)
+    router.init(secondary)
+
+    expect(router.app).toBe(main)
+    expect(router.apps.length).toBe(2)
+
+    main.$destroy()
+
+
+    expect(router.apps.length).toBe(1)
+    expect(router.apps.indexOf(main)).toBe(-1)
+    expect(router.apps[0]).toBe(secondary)
+
+    expect(router.app).toBe(secondary)
+    expect(router.app).not.toBe(null)
+  })
+
+  it('leaves router.app intact when a non-main app is destroyed', () => {
+    const router = newRouter()
+    const main = createMockApp(1)
+    const secondary = createMockApp(2)
+
+    router.init(main)
+    router.init(secondary)
+
+    secondary.$destroy()
+
+    expect(router.apps.length).toBe(1)
+    expect(router.apps[0]).toBe(main)
+    expect(router.app).toBe(main)
+  })
+
+  it('does not accumulate destroyed apps across many create/destroy cycles', () => {
+
+
+
+    const router = newRouter()
+    const first = createMockApp(0)
+    router.init(first)
+
+    for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) {
+      const next = createMockApp(i)
+      router.init(next)
+
+      next.$destroy()
+    }
+
+
+    expect(router.apps.length).toBe(1)
+    expect(router.apps[0]).toBe(first)
+    expect(router.app).toBe(first)
+  })

+  it('handles destroying multiple apps sequentially down to empty', () => {

+    const b = createMockApp(2)
+    const c = createMockApp(3)

+import { VDataTable } from '../VDataTable'
+
+
+import { describe, expect, it } from '@jest/globals'
+import { mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
+import { createVuetify } from '@/framework'
+
+const HEADERS = [
+  { key: 'cat', title: 'Cat' },
+  { key: 'name', title: 'Name' },
+]
+
+const ITEMS = [
+  { id: 1, cat: 'b', name: 'z' },
+  { id: 2, cat: 'a', name: 'y' },
+  { id: 3, cat: 'b', name: 'w' },
+  { id: 4, cat: 'a', name: 'x' },
+]
+
+function mountAndCaptureItems (props: Record<string, any>) {
+  const vuetify = createVuetify()
+  let captured: any = null
+  mount<any>(VDataTable, {
+    props,
+    slots: {
+      body: (slotProps: any) => {
+        captured = slotProps.items
+        return ''
+      },
+    },
+    global: { plugins: [vuetify] },
+  })
+  return captured as any[]
+}
+
+describe('VDataTable - disable-sort + group-by', () => {
+
+
+  it('groups items by groupBy key (asc) when disable-sort is true', () => {
+    const items = mountAndCaptureItems({
+      items: ITEMS,
+      headers: HEADERS,
+      groupBy: [{ key: 'cat', order: 'asc' }],
+      disableSort: true,
+    })
+
+    expect(items).not.toBeNull()
+    expect(items).toHaveLength(4)
+
+    expect(items.map((i: any) => i.cat)).toStrictEqual(['a', 'a', 'b', 'b'])
+  })
+
+
+
+  it('does NOT apply sortBy when disable-sort is true and there is no groupBy', () => {
+    const items = mountAndCaptureItems({
+      items: ITEMS,
+      headers: HEADERS,
+      sortBy: [{ key: 'name', order: 'asc' }],
+      disableSort: true,
+    })
+
+
+    expect(items.map((i: any) => i.id)).toStrictEqual([1, 2, 3, 4])
+  })
+
+
+
+  it('groups by groupBy but does NOT apply sortBy within groups when disable-sort', () => {
+    const items = mountAndCaptureItems({
+      items: ITEMS,
+      headers: HEADERS,
+      groupBy: [{ key: 'cat', order: 'asc' }],
+      sortBy: [{ key: 'name', order: 'asc' }],
+      disableSort: true,
+    })
+
+    expect(items).toHaveLength(4)
+
+    expect(items.map((i: any) => i.cat)).toStrictEqual(['a', 'a', 'b', 'b'])
+
+
+
+
+    expect(items.map((i: any) => i.name)).toStrictEqual(['y', 'x', 'z', 'w'])
+  })
+
+
+  it('sorts by sortBy normally when disable-sort is false', () => {
+    const items = mountAndCaptureItems({

+    parsed = parse_qs(

+    )
+    for key, value in expected.items():
+        assert parsed.get(key) == [value]
+
+
+def assert_required_headers(headers):
+
+    assert headers["Content-type"] == "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
+    assert headers["User-agent"] == "reCAPTCHA Django"
+

+def normalize_request_args(args, kwargs):
+
+    normalized = dict(kwargs)
+    for name, value in zip(("url", "data", "headers"), args):
+        normalized.setdefault(name, value)
+    return normalized
+

+def patch_request_stack(monkeypatch, request_cls, build_opener_func, proxy_handler_cls=None):
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(client, "Request", request_cls, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(urllib_request, "Request", request_cls)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(client, "build_opener", build_opener_func, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(urllib_request, "build_opener", build_opener_func)
+    if proxy_handler_cls is not None:
+        monkeypatch.setattr(client, "ProxyHandler", proxy_handler_cls, raising=False)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(urllib_request, "ProxyHandler", proxy_handler_cls)
+

+    fake_response = FakeHTTPResponse(body)

+    class FakeRequest:
+        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            request_kwargs = normalize_request_args(args, kwargs)
+            if captured is not None:

+                captured["request_kwargs"] = request_kwargs

+package abi
+
+import (
+	"math/big"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+)
+
+
+
+func TestTopicEncodingRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		Type string
+		Val  interface{}
+	}{
+		{"bool", true},
+		{"bool", false},
+		{"uint8", uint8(255)},
+		{"uint16", uint16(65535)},
+		{"uint32", uint32(1)},
+		{"uint64", uint64(20)},
+		{"uint256", big.NewInt(1000000)},
+		{"int8", int8(-1)},
+		{"int32", int32(-12345)},
+		{"int64", int64(-987654321)},
+		{"int256", big.NewInt(-1000000)},
+		{"address", [20]byte{0x1, 0x2, 0x3}},
+	}
+
+	for _, c := range cases {
+		tt, err := NewType(c.Type)
+		assert.NoError(t, err)
+
+		word, err := EncodeTopic(tt, c.Val)
+		assert.NoError(t, err)
+
+		got, err := ParseTopic(tt, word)
+		assert.NoError(t, err)
+
+		assert.Equal(t, c.Val, got, "round trip failed for type %s", c.Type)
+	}
+}
+
+
+func TestTopicEncodingLayout(t *testing.T) {
+
+	boolT, _ := NewType("bool")
+	word, err := EncodeTopic(boolT, true)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	var expectedTrue [32]byte
+	expectedTrue[31] = 1
+	assert.Equal(t, expectedTrue, word)
+
+	word, err = EncodeTopic(boolT, false)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, [32]byte{}, word)
+
+
+	u64T, _ := NewType("uint64")
+	word, err = EncodeTopic(u64T, uint64(20))
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	var expectedNum [32]byte
+	expectedNum[31] = 20
+	assert.Equal(t, expectedNum, word)
+
+
+	addrT, _ := NewType("address")
+	addr := [20]byte{0x11, 0x22, 0x33}
+	word, err = EncodeTopic(addrT, addr)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	for i := 0; i < 12; i++ {
+		assert.Equal(t, byte(0), word[i])
+	}
+	assert.Equal(t, addr[:], word[12:])
+}
+
+
+
+func TestTopicParseTypes(t *testing.T) {
+	u8T, _ := NewType("uint8")
+	word, err := EncodeTopic(u8T, uint8(10))
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	got, err := ParseTopic(u8T, word)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, uint8(10), got)
+
+	i32T, _ := NewType("int32")
+	word, err = EncodeTopic(i32T, int32(-1))
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	got, err = ParseTopic(i32T, word)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, int32(-1), got)
+
+	u256T, _ := NewType("uint256")
+	word, err = EncodeTopic(u256T, big.NewInt(123456789))
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	got, err = ParseTopic(u256T, word)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, big.NewInt(123456789), got)
+
+	addrT, _ := NewType("address")
+	addr := [20]byte{0xaa, 0xbb}
+	word, err = EncodeTopic(addrT, addr)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	got, err = ParseTopic(addrT, word)
+	assert.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, addr, got)
+}
+
+
+
+func TestTopicUnsupportedTypes(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, typ := range []string{"string", "bytes", "bytes32", "uint256[]", "uint8[2]"} {
+		tt, err := NewType(typ)
+		assert.NoError(t, err)
+
+		_, err = EncodeTopic(tt, "anything")
+		assert.Error(t, err, "EncodeTopic should reject type %s", typ)
+
+		_, err = ParseTopic(tt, [32]byte{})
+		assert.Error(t, err, "ParseTopic should reject type %s", typ)
+	}
+}
+
+
+
+func TestTopicInvalidBool(t *testing.T) {
+	boolT, _ := NewType("bool")
+
+	var word [32]byte
+	word[0] = 0x5
+	_, err := ParseTopic(boolT, word)
+	assert.Error(t, err)
+
+
+	var word2 [32]byte
+	word2[31] = 0x2
+	_, err = ParseTopic(boolT, word2)
+	assert.Error(t, err)
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from src.app import Erys
+from src.cell import Cell
+from src.notebook import Notebook
+
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+
+
+class ProbeErys(Erys):
+    CSS_PATH = str(REPO_ROOT / "src" / "styles.tcss")
+
+    def __init__(self, paths: list[Path]) -> None:
+        super().__init__(paths)
+        self.probe_notices: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+
+    def notify(
+        self,
+        message: str,
+        *,
+        title: str = "",
+        severity: str = "information",
+        timeout: float | None = None,
+        markup: bool = True,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.probe_notices.append(
+            {
+                "markup": markup,
+                "message": str(message),
+                "severity": severity,
+                "timeout": timeout,
+                "title": str(title),
+            }
+        )
+        return super().notify(
+            message,
+            title=title,
+            severity=severity,
+            timeout=timeout,
+            markup=markup,
+        )
+
+
+class FixtureKernel:
+    initialized = False
+
+    def get_kernel_info(self) -> dict[str, str]:
+        return {"name": "fixture-kernel"}
+
+    def get_kernel_spec(self) -> dict[str, str]:
+        return {
+            "display_name": "Fixture Python",
+            "language": "python",
+            "name": "fixture-python",
+        }
+
+    def get_language_info(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "file_extension": ".py",
+            "mimetype": "text/x-python",
+            "name": "python",
+            "pygments_lexer": "ipython3",
+            "version": "3.12-fixture",
+        }
+
+
+def canonical(value: Any) -> str:
+    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
+
+
+def cell_summary(cell: Cell) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "class": type(cell).__name__,
+        "editable": bool(getattr(cell, "input_text", None))
+        and not bool(getattr(cell.input_text, "read_only", False)),
+        "exec_count": getattr(cell, "exec_count", None),
+        "id": getattr(cell, "_cell_id", None),
+        "next": getattr(cell.next, "_cell_id", None),
+        "outputs": getattr(cell, "outputs", None),
+        "prev": getattr(cell.prev, "_cell_id", None),
+        "source": cell.input_text.text,
+        "type": cell.cell_type,
+    }
+
+
+async def settle(pilot) -> None:
+    await pilot.pause(0.5)
+    await pilot.pause(0.5)
+
+
+def disable_kernel_startup() -> None:
+    os.environ.pop("VIRTUAL_ENV", None)
+    os.environ.pop("CONDA_PREFIX", None)
+
+
+def assert_required_saved_notebook(saved_json: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+
+    required_top_level = {"metadata", "nbformat", "nbformat_minor", "cells"}
+    missing = required_top_level - set(saved_json)
+    assert not missing, f"saved notebook missing top-level fields: {sorted(missing)}"
+    assert isinstance(saved_json["metadata"], dict), "saved metadata must be an object"
+    assert isinstance(saved_json["cells"], list), "saved cells must be an array"
+
+
+    for key in ["kernel_info", "kernel_spec", "language_info"]:
+        assert key in saved_json["metadata"], f"saved metadata missing {key}"
+        assert isinstance(saved_json["metadata"][key], dict), f"{key} must be an object"
+
+
+def assert_saved_cells_match_editor(
+    saved_json: dict[str, Any], cells: list[Cell]
+) -> None:
+
+    assert len(saved_json["cells"]) == len(cells), "saved cell count must match editor"
+    for idx, (saved_cell, editor_cell) in enumerate(zip(saved_json["cells"], cells)):
+        assert saved_cell.get("cell_type") == editor_cell.cell_type, (
+            f"saved cell {idx} type does not match editor"
+        )
+        assert saved_cell.get("source") == editor_cell.input_text.text, (
+            f"saved cell {idx} source does not match editor"
+        )
+
+
+def assert_loaded_cells(cells: list[Cell], expected: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
+
+    assert len(cells) == len(expected), "loaded notebook cell count mismatch"
+    for idx, (cell, want) in enumerate(zip(cells, expected)):
+        assert cell.cell_type == want["cell_type"], f"loaded cell {idx} type mismatch"
+        assert cell.input_text.text == want["source"], f"loaded cell {idx} source mismatch"
+        assert not getattr(cell.input_text, "read_only", False), (
+            f"loaded cell {idx} is not editable"
+        )
+
+
+async def valid_open_save(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
+    disable_kernel_startup()

+        await settle(pilot)
+        notebook = app.switcher.q

+import json
+import os
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression, Ridge
+
+from banditml_pkg.banditml.preprocessing import preprocessor
+from banditml_pkg.banditml.serving.predictor import BanditPredictor
+from utils import model_constructors
+
+
+EXPERIMENT = {
+    "features": {
+        "age": {"type": "N"},
+        "decision": {"type": "C", "possible_values": ["left", "right"]},
+    },
+    "product_sets": {},
+}
+
+
+def prepared_training_data(binary=False):
+    rows = []
+    for age, decision in enumerate(["left", "right", "left", "right", "left", "right"]):
+        reward = int(age >= 3) if binary else float(age * 2 + (decision == "right"))
+        rows.append(
+            {
+                "context": json.dumps({"age": age}),
+                "decision": decision,
+                "immediate_reward": json.dumps({"reward": reward}),
+                "delayed_reward": json.dumps(
+                    {"left": {"reward": 0}, "right": {"reward": 0}}
+                ),
+            }
+        )
+    raw = pd.DataFrame(rows)
+    return preprocessor.preprocess_data(
+        raw, {"reward": 1}, EXPERIMENT, shuffle_data=False
+    )
+
+
+def make_predictor(model, data, reward_type):
+    return BanditPredictor(
+        experiment_params=EXPERIMENT,
+        float_feature_order=data["float_feature_order"],
+        id_feature_order=data["id_feature_order"],
+        id_feature_str_to_int_map=data["id_feature_str_to_int_map"],
+        transforms=data["transforms"],
+        imputers=data["imputers"],
+        model=model,
+        reward_type=reward_type,
+    )
+
+
+class TestSklearnPredictorSupport(unittest.TestCase):
+    def assert_serves_estimator(self, model, reward_type, binary=False):
+        data = prepared_training_data(binary=binary)
+        model.fit(data["X_float"], data["y"])
+        predictor = make_predictor(model, data, reward_type)
+        context = {"age": 2}
+
+        prepared = predictor.preprocess_input(context)
+        if binary:
+            expected = model.predict_proba(prepared["X_float"])[:, 1]
+        else:
+            expected = model.predict(prepared["X_float"])
+        try:
+            served = predictor.predict(context)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.fail("sklearn estimator could not be served: %r" % (exc,))
+
+        self.assertEqual(served["ids"], ["left", "right"])
+        self.assertEqual(np.asarray(served["scores"]).shape, (2, 1))
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(np.asarray(served["scores"]).ravel(), expected)
+
+    def test_regression_estimators_are_scored(self):
+        self.assert_serves_estimator(Ridge(alpha=1.0), "regression")
+        self.assert_serves_estimator(
+            model_constructors.build_gbdt("regression", 0.1, 8, 2), "regression"
+        )
+        self.assert_serves_estimator(
+            model_constructors.build_random_forest("regression", 8, 2), "regression"
+        )
+
+    def test_binary_estimators_return_positive_class_scores(self):
+        self.assert_serves_estimator(
+            LogisticRegression(penalty="l2"), "binary", binary=True
+        )
+        self.assert_serves_estimator(
+            model_constructors.build_gbdt("binary", 0.1, 8, 2), "binary", binary=True
+        )
+        self.assert_serves_estimator(
+            model_constructors.build_random_forest("binary", 8, 2), "binary", binary=True
+        )
+
+    def test_sklearn_regression_round_trip(self):
+        data = prepared_training_data()
+        model = Ridge(alpha=1.0).fit(data["X_float"], data["y"])
+        predictor = make_predictor(model, data, "regression")
+        context = {"age": 4}
+        before = predictor.predict(context)
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            config_path = os.path.join(directory, "model.json")
+            model_path = os.path.join(directory, "model.bin")
+            predictor.config_to_file(config_path)
+            predictor.model_to_file(model_path)
+            restored = BanditPredictor.predictor_from_file(config_path, model_path)
+            after = restored.predict(context)
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(after["scores"], before["scores"])
+        self.assertEqual(after["ids"], before["ids"])
+
+    def test_sklearn_binary_round_trip(self):
+        data = prepared_training_data(binary=True)
+        model = LogisticRegression(penalty="l2").fit(data["X_float"], data["y"])
+        predictor = make_predictor(model, data, "binary")
+        context = {"age": 1}
+        before = predictor.predict(context)
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+            config_path = os.path.join(directory, "model.json")
+            model_path = os.path.join(directory, "model.bin")
+            predictor.config_to_file(config_path)
+            predictor.model_to_file(model_path)
+            restored = BanditPredictor.predictor_from_file(config_path, model_path)
+            after = restored.predict(context)
+        np.testing.assert_allclose(after["scores"], before["scores"])
+        self.assertEqual(after["ids"], before["ids"])

+from dbt.semver import (
+    VersionSpecifier,
+    find_possible_versions,
+    reduce_versions,
+    resolve_to_specific_version,
+    versions_compatible,
+)
+
+
+def test_semver_prerelease_precedence_chain():
+    ordered = [
+        '1.0.0-alpha',
+        '1.0.0-alpha.1',
+        '1.0.0-alpha.beta',
+        '1.0.0-beta',
+        '1.0.0-beta.2',
+        '1.0.0-beta.11',
+        '1.0.0-rc.1',
+        '1.0.0',
+    ]
+
+    for lower, higher in zip(ordered, ordered[1:]):
+        assert VersionSpecifier.from_version_string(lower).compare(
+            VersionSpecifier.from_version_string(higher)
+        ) == -1
+
+
+def test_semver_numeric_core_precedence():
+    assert VersionSpecifier.from_version_string('1.0.0').compare(
+        VersionSpecifier.from_version_string('1.1.0')
+    ) == -1
+    assert VersionSpecifier.from_version_string('1.1.0').compare(
+        VersionSpecifier.from_version_string('2.0.0')
+    ) == -1
+
+
+def test_exact_versions_use_prerelease_precedence():
+    assert not versions_compatible('1.0.0-alpha', '1.0.0')
+
+
+def test_range_bounds_use_prerelease_precedence():
+    assert not versions_compatible('>=1.0.0', '1.0.0-beta')
+    assert not versions_compatible('<=1.0.0-alpha', '1.0.0-alpha.1')
+    assert versions_compatible('>1.0.0-alpha', '1.0.0-alpha.1')
+
+
+def test_build_metadata_is_ignored_for_precedence_and_exact_compatibility():
+    first = VersionSpecifier.from_version_string('1.0.0+linux')
+    second = VersionSpecifier.from_version_string('1.0.0+macos')
+    assert first.compare(second) == 0
+    assert versions_compatible('1.0.0+linux', '1.0.0+macos')
+
+
+def test_find_possible_versions_filters_prereleases_and_sorts_semantically():
+    stable_range = reduce_versions('>=1.0.0')
+    assert find_possible_versions(
+        stable_range,
+        ['1.0.0-beta', '0.9.9', '1.0.0', '1.0.0-alpha'],
+    ) == ['1.0.0']
+
+    prerelease_range = reduce_versions('>=1.0.0-alpha')
+    assert find_possible_versions(
+        prerelease_range,
+        ['1.0.0-alpha', '1.0.0', '1.0.0-beta'],
+    ) == ['1.0.0', '1.0.0-beta', '1.0.0-alpha']
+
+
+def test_resolver_chooses_highest_precedence_and_keeps_original_text():
+    requested = reduce_versions('>=1.0.0-alpha')
+    assert resolve_to_specific_version(
+        requested,
+        ['1.0.0-alpha', '1.0.0-beta', '1.0.0+linux'],
+    ) == '1.0.0+linux'

+
+
+
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from monai.metrics import LossMetric
+
+
+def _assert_close(testcase, actual, expected):
+    testcase.assertIsInstance(actual, torch.Tensor)
+    expected = expected.to(device=actual.device, dtype=actual.dtype)
+    if actual.numel() != expected.numel():
+        testcase.assertEqual(tuple(actual.shape), tuple(expected.shape))
+    testcase.assertTrue(torch.allclose(actual.reshape(-1), expected.reshape(-1), equal_nan=True), f"{actual} != {expected}")
+
+
+class TestLossMetric(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_public_import_iteration_return_and_accumulation(self):
+        def per_sample_mean(y_pred):
+            return y_pred.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+
+        metric = LossMetric(loss_fn=per_sample_mean, reduction="mean")
+
+        first = torch.tensor([[1.0, 3.0], [5.0, 7.0]])
+        second = torch.tensor([[2.0, 8.0]])
+
+        expected_first = torch.tensor([[2.0], [6.0]])
+        expected_second = torch.tensor([[5.0]])
+
+        first_result = metric(first)
+        second_result = metric(second)
+
+        _assert_close(self, first_result, expected_first)
+        _assert_close(self, second_result, expected_second)
+
+        expected_all = torch.cat([expected_first, expected_second], dim=0)
+        aggregated = metric.aggregate(reduction="none")
+        _assert_close(self, aggregated, expected_all)
+
+    def test_prediction_only_and_prediction_with_label_call_signatures(self):
+        pred_only_calls = []
+
+        def pred_only_loss(*args):
+            pred_only_calls.append(len(args))
+            return args[0].sum().reshape(1, 1)
+
+        label_calls = []
+
+        def pred_and_label_loss(*args):
+            label_calls.append(len(args))
+            y_pred, y = args
+            return (y_pred - y).abs().sum().reshape(1, 1)
+
+        y_pred = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0, 4.0]])
+        y = torch.tensor([[0.5, 3.0, 1.0]])
+
+        pred_only_result = LossMetric(loss_fn=pred_only_loss)(y_pred)
+        self.assertEqual(pred_only_calls, [1])
+        _assert_close(self, pred_only_result, torch.tensor([[7.0]]))
+
+        label_result = LossMetric(loss_fn=pred_and_label_loss)(y_pred, y)
+        self.assertEqual(label_calls, [2])
+        _assert_close(self, label_result, torch.tensor([[4.5]]))
+
+    def test_scalar_and_vector_loss_outputs_are_batch_first_compatible(self):
+        scalar_metric = LossMetric(loss_fn=lambda x: x.mean(), reduction="none")
+
+        scalar_first = scalar_metric(torch.tensor([2.0, 3.0]))
+        scalar_second = scalar_metric(torch.tensor([4.0, 6.0]))
+
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(scalar_first.ndim, 2)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(scalar_second.ndim, 2)
+        _assert_close(self, scalar_first, torch.tensor([[2.5]]))
+        _assert_close(self, scalar_second, torch.tensor([[5.0]]))
+
+        scalar_aggregate = scalar_metric.aggregate(reduction="none")
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(scalar_aggregate.ndim, 2)
+        _assert_close(self, scalar_aggregate, torch.tensor([[2.5], [5.0]]))
+
+        def vector_loss(x):
+            return torch.stack([x.sum(), x.mean()])
+
+        vector_metric = LossMetric(loss_fn=vector_loss, reduction="mean")
+        vector_metric(torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0]))
+        vector_metric(torch.tensor([3.0, 5.0]))
+
+        _assert_close(self, vector_metric.aggregate(reduction="none"), torch.tensor([[3.0, 1.5], [8.0, 4.0]]))
+        _assert_close(self, vector_metric.aggregate(reduction="mean"), torch.tensor(4.125))
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _expected_reductions(data):
+        return {
+            "none": data,
+            "mean": data.mean(),
+            "sum": data.sum(),
+            "mean_batch": data.mean(dim=0),
+            "sum_batch": data.sum(dim=0),
+            "mean_channel": data.mean(dim=1),
+            "sum_channel": data.sum(dim=1),
+        }
+
+    def _run_reduction_case(self, first, second):
+        calls = [first.clone(), second.clone()]
+
+        def queued_loss(_):
+            return calls.pop(0)
+
+        metric = LossMetric(loss_fn=queued_loss, reduction="sum")
+        metric(torch.zeros(first.shape[0], 1))
+        metric(torch.zeros(second.shape[0], 1))
+
+        all_data = torch.cat([first, second], dim=0)
+        expected = self._expected_reductions(all_data)
+
+        for reduction, expected_value in expected.items():
+            with self.subTest(reduction=reduction, data=all_data.tolist()):
+                _assert_close(self, metric.aggregate(reduction=reduction), expected_value)
+
+        _assert_close(self, metric.aggregate(reduction="mean"), expected["mean"])
+        _assert_close(self, metric.aggregate(), expected["sum"])
+
+    def test_reduction_modes_and_aggregate_override(self):
+        cases = [
+            (torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]), torch.tensor([[5.0, 8.0]])),
+            (torch.tensor([[2.0, 6.0], [4.0, 10.0]]), torch.tensor([[8.0, 12.0]])),
+        ]

+
+        default_metric = LossMetric(loss_fn=loss_fn, reduction="none")

+        not_nan_metric(torch.zeros(2, 1))

+                "conditions": conditions,
+                "conditions_match_logic": logic,
+            }
+        }
+    }

+

+def test_text_aliases_and_all_any_logic_are_consistent():
+    text = "Welcome to the status page"
+    result = evaluate(

+        "ANY",
+    )
+    assert any_result["result"] is True
+
+    all_result = evaluate(
+        [
+            {"operator": "==", "field": "page_text", "value": text},
+            {"operator": "==", "field": "page_text", "value": "does not match"},
+        ],
+        text,
+        "bogus",
+    )
+    assert all_result["result"] is False
+
+
+def test_incomplete_rows_are_ignored_without_changing_complete_rules():
+    result = evaluate(
+        [
+            {"operator": "==", "field": "page_text", "value": "ready"},
+            {"operator": "==", "field": "page_text"},
+            {"operator": "", "field": "page_text", "value": "ignored"},
+        ],
+        "ready",
+    )
+    assert result["result"] is True
+
+    only_incomplete = evaluate([{"operator": "==", "value": "ready"}], "ready")
+    assert only_incomplete["result"] is True
+
+
+def test_invalid_regex_is_a_failed_condition_instead_of_an_exception():
+    positive = evaluate(
+        [{"operator": "contains_regex", "field": "page_text", "value": "["}],
+        "anything",
+    )
+    assert positive["result"] is False
+
+    negative = evaluate(
+        [{"operator": "!contains_regex", "field": "page_text", "value": "["}],
+        "anything",
+    )
+    assert negative["result"] is False
+
+
+def test_zero_price_is_numeric_and_missing_price_does_not_leak_state():
+    zero = evaluate(
+        [{"operator": "==", "field": "extracted_number", "value": "0"}],
+        "Current price: $0",
+    )
+    assert zero["result"] is True
+    assert zero["executed_data"]["extracted_number"] == 0.0
+
+    missing = evaluate(
+        [{"operator": "==", "field": "extracted_number", "value": "0"}],
+        "Nothing to see here",
+    )
+    assert missing["result"] is False
+    assert "extracted_number" not in missing["executed_data"]
